title: Bind from chroot with O_PATH
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

> /kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Using `O_PATH` does not grant read or write access to files or directories upon opening, making the opened `/proc/self/df/N` less useful, as they have no permissions. This allows simplifying the difference between files and directories.

The fix is specifically for files, but I opted to add it for both files and directories, let me know if you prefer to revert.

With the previous `O_RDRW`, we couldn't mount twice the same file in two parallel stage if one of the stage is executing the file and would receive a `ETXTBSY` error instead.

As far as I can tell we do not need the file to be read-write since the writeability of the layer is handled via an overlay anyhow.

It should keep the same safety as what the original code was guarding against (https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2024-11218) as far as I can tell, and is close to what Buildkit is doing in https://github.com/moby/buildkit/blob/master/executor/oci/spec_linux.go#L338.

Note that BuildKit also sets `O_CLOEXEC`, which is probably a good idea, but would need to be set in open_unix.go as `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC`. I have not done that change for now, but can add it too if you prefer.

#### How to verify it

See the tests

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #7162

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Properly support mounting the same file in separate stages while one of the stage executes the file
```
